_doc: Host-side Waydroid resource policy (consumed by configuration_containers.nix). The Android workload runs in the LXC container cgroup (top-level lxc.pivot tree), NOT under waydroid-container.service's cgroup — so a systemd CPUQuota/AllowedCPUs on the service does NOT constrain it. The cap must be an LXC cgroup2 directive injected into the generated config (config_base). We use cpu.max (bandwidth) rather than cpuset.cpus (pinning): cpu.max cannot fail container start (no cpuset parent-delegation dependency), and per-period throttling frees ALL cores when the quota is spent, so the desktop is never starved for a whole period.

cgroup._doc: cpu.max = '<quota_us> <period_us>'. quota = cpu_max_cores * cpu_period_us. The SP8 has 8 logical CPUs; capping at 7 leaves >=1 core of headroom so a runaway Android workload can never peg all 8 and freeze the machine.
